input.strategy_title: Keyboard accessibility conformance for core Dashboard flows
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

An accessibility audit found that four core Dashboard flows (project creation,
workbench spawn, model deployment, pipeline run submission) cannot be completed
with keyboard alone: focus is lost in modals, several controls are unreachable,
and focus indicators are inconsistent. Two public-sector customers require an
updated, published conformance statement (VPAT) before renewal — so the fixes
and the published documentation are both deliverables of this strategy.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P1 | The four audited core flows are fully operable by keyboard, with no focus traps or unreachable controls. |
| HLR-2 | P1 | Visible focus indicators are consistent across the audited flows. |
| HLR-3 | P2 | The accessibility conformance documentation (VPAT and product docs accessibility statement) is updated and republished to reflect the fixed state, with technical review. |

## Affected Components

- Dashboard
- Documentation

## Out of Scope

- Screen-reader semantics beyond what the keyboard fixes require
- Flows outside the four audited ones

## Open Questions

None — the audit report enumerates the exact defects per flow.

# Keyboard accessibility remediation for core Dashboard flows

## Description

This epic remediates the keyboard-accessibility defects that the accessibility
audit enumerated in the four core Dashboard flows — project creation, workbench
spawn, model deployment, and pipeline run submission. The audit found that focus
is lost in modals, several controls are unreachable by keyboard, and focus
indicators are inconsistent. This epic delivers all four flows fully operable
by keyboard alone, with no focus traps, no unreachable controls, and consistent
visible focus indication.

## Scope

- Remediate every keyboard-operability defect the audit enumerated in the four
  audited flows: focus loss and focus traps in modals and dialogs, and controls
  that cannot be reached or activated with keyboard input.
- Apply a consistent, visible focus indicator to all interactive controls
  across the four audited flows, replacing the inconsistent indicator styles
  the audit found.
- Include screen-reader semantics only where the keyboard fixes require them;
  broader screen-reader work is out of scope.
- Flows outside the four audited ones are out of scope.
- Verification of the fixes per flow (keyboard walkthrough or scripted
  keyboard-traversal checks against the audit's defect list).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Each of the four audited flows (project creation, workbench spawn, model
  deployment, pipeline run submission) can be completed end-to-end using
  keyboard input alone, with no step that requires a pointing device.
- Every interactive control exposed in the audited flows is reachable by
  keyboard traversal and operable by keyboard activation.
- No focus traps remain in the audited flows: focus can always leave modals
  and dialogs, and focus returns to the invoking element when they close.
- Focus is visibly indicated on all interactive controls in the audited flows,
  with one consistent indicator style across all four flows.
- Every defect enumerated in the audit report for the four flows is verified
  fixed, with the verification recorded per defect.
- The functional behavior of the four flows is unchanged apart from the
  accessibility remediation (no regressions introduced).

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-1 (P1)** — the four audited core flows are fully operable by keyboard,
  with no focus traps or unreachable controls: covered by this epic.
- **HLR-2 (P1)** — visible focus indicators are consistent across the audited
  flows: covered by this epic. Bundled with HLR-1 rather than split: both HLRs
  are remediated in a single pass over the same four flows in the same
  component and team — the audit's defect list interleaves focus traps,
  unreachable controls, and inconsistent indicators per flow, so a split would
  force two passes over the same UI surfaces and add an artificial
  serialization edge between epics building the same surface.

# Update and republish accessibility conformance documentation

## Description

This epic updates the published accessibility conformance documentation to
reflect the remediated state of the four core Dashboard flows: the VPAT
conformance statement and the product documentation accessibility statement.
Both artifacts are updated and republished through the Red Hat docs content
process, with technical review against the implemented keyboard fixes. This
satisfies the public-sector customers' requirement for an updated, published
conformance statement.

## Scope

- Update the VPAT conformance statement entries for the four audited flows
  (project creation, workbench spawn, model deployment, pipeline run
  submission) to reflect the remediated keyboard operability and focus-indicator
  support.
- Update the product documentation accessibility statement to reflect the fixed
  state.
- Republish both artifacts through the Red Hat docs content process.
- Claims are scoped to what was implemented and verified: keyboard operability
  and focus indication in the four audited flows. Flows outside the four
  audited ones and screen-reader semantics beyond what the keyboard fixes
  require are not claimed as conformant.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The VPAT is updated to reflect the remediated state of the four audited
  flows and is republished.
- The product documentation accessibility statement is updated to reflect the
  fixed state and is republished.
- The updated documentation is technically reviewed against the implemented
  keyboard fixes, with the review recorded (claims checked against the
  delivered remediation and its verification results).
- No conformance claim in the updated artifacts extends beyond the implemented
  and verified keyboard fixes in the four audited flows.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-3 (P2)** — the accessibility conformance documentation (VPAT and
  product docs accessibility statement) is updated and republished to reflect
  the fixed state, with technical review: covered by this epic.

# Decomposition Summary — RHAISTRAT-9017

Keyboard accessibility conformance for core Dashboard flows.

## Triage

Not below-threshold and not docs-only: the strategy spans two components and two
architecturally distinct work streams — code remediation in the Dashboard (four
audited flows) and substantive content authoring in Documentation (VPAT and
accessibility statement update and republish). Full decomposition follows.

## Epic List

| ID | Title | Type | Team | Priority |
|----|-------|------|------|----------|
| RHAISTRAT-9017-E001 | Keyboard accessibility remediation for core Dashboard flows | Implementation | RHOAI Dashboard | P1 |
| RHAISTRAT-9017-E002 | Update and republish accessibility conformance documentation (VPAT and accessibility statement) | Implementation (docs-authoring) | RHOAI Documentation | P2 |

## Dependency DAG

```mermaid
graph TD
    E001[RHAISTRAT-9017-E001 Keyboard accessibility remediation] --> E002[RHAISTRAT-9017-E002 Conformance documentation update]
```

## DAG Justification

| Edge | Rule | Rationale |
|------|------|-----------|
| E001 → E002 | Rule 11 (docs-authoring blocked by ALL Implementation epics) | The VPAT and accessibility statement describe the fixed state, so the documentation cannot be authored or technically reviewed until the keyboard remediation is complete. |

**Parallel non-edges:** none — with a single implementation epic there is no
parallelizable pair. No konflux-onboarding, repo-onboarding, or
license-validation epic is generated: Dashboard is an existing, Konflux-onboarded
component (see `architecture/rhoai-3.0/dashboard.md`) and no new component or
container image is introduced.

## HLR Traceability Matrix

| HLR | Priority | Epic(s) | Notes |
|-----|----------|---------|-------|
| HLR-1 — four audited flows fully operable by keyboard, no focus traps or unreachable controls | P1 | RHAISTRAT-9017-E001 | Primary scope of the Dashboard remediation epic. |
| HLR-2 — visible focus indicators consistent across the audited flows | P1 | RHAISTRAT-9017-E001 | Bundled with HLR-1: both HLRs are remediated by a single pass over the same four flows in the same component and team — the audit's defect list interleaves focus traps, unreachable controls, and inconsistent indicators per flow, so splitting would force two passes over the same UI surfaces and an artificial serialization edge between epics building the same surface. |
| HLR-3 — conformance documentation (VPAT and accessibility statement) updated, republished, with technical review | P2 | RHAISTRAT-9017-E002 | Substantive content authoring in the Documentation component — separate work stream and review cycle from the code fixes. Priority P2 per the docs-authoring exception (strategy frontmatter `priority: Normal`). |

All three HLRs are covered; no orphaned requirements.

## Component Mapping

`Dashboard` and `Documentation` are both verbatim canonical names from
`.context/rhai-components.txt` — no non-obvious mappings.

## Health Warnings

- **Missing strategy sections**: the strategy has no Impacted Teams table, no
  Dependencies table, no Acceptance Criteria (Given/When/Then) section, and no
  Non-Functional Requirements section. Decomposition proceeded from the HLR
  table and problem statement. The Dashboard owning team (RHOAI Dashboard) was
  taken from `architecture/rhoai-3.0/dashboard.md`; no source establishes the
  Documentation epic's owner, so "RHOAI Documentation" is an assumption that
  should be confirmed at plan review.
- **AC derivation**: with no Given/When/Then acceptance criteria in the
  strategy, epic ACs were derived from the HLRs and the audit's enumerated
  defect categories. The audit report itself (referenced but not attached) is
  the authoritative defect list and should be attached to the implementation
  epic in Jira.
- **E001 size / conditional re-split trigger**: the epic is one logical change
  (a single mechanical sweep of the audit's enumerated defect list over the four
  audited flows, same component and team) sized at roughly the two-week line, so
  it is not split now. Re-split trigger: if remediation of any single flow
  exceeds 3 engineering days, or the sweep as a whole exceeds 10 engineering
  days, split the epic along flow boundaries (one epic per audited flow, or
  flows grouped under that budget), since the four flows are independent UI
  surfaces and can be remediated in parallel once the defect list is enumerated
  per flow.
- **Customer-driven deadline risk**: two public-sector customers require the
  republished VPAT before renewal — a schedule pressure on the chain, not a
  structural constraint; it does not change the DAG.
- No priority inversions detected (P1 code remediation precedes P2
  documentation, consistent with Rule 11 ordering).

## Tiered Delivery

Not applicable — no external dependency with uncertain timing; the strategy has
no dependencies table and no open questions.
